proposed: [SYNTHETIC] Example Tower Ltd misses interest payment on 70,000 sq ft City office
[SYNTHETIC] AI firm signs 15-year lease on 60,000 sq ft near King's Cross
[SYNTHETIC] Refurbishments dominate Q3 2026 starts; 2027-28 Grade A deliveries 32% below average

runs.answer:
**No opportunities worth proposing this week.** All five investigated candidates were either duplicates of cards already pending with you or failed review.

**Already on your desk** — three of this week's stories came back as duplicates of cards you've already seen (cards 1, 3 and 4, pending): the thinning Grade A pipeline — refurbishments were 91% of central London office construction starts in Q3 2026, no ground-up schemes started, and new Grade A deliveries in 2027-28 are expected to run 32% below average [D188#0]; the Example Tower owner missing an interest payment on its 70,000 sq ft City office with its lender reviewing options [D191#0]; and Example AI Labs agreeing a 15-year lease on 60,000 sq ft of new Grade A offices near King's Cross [D187#0].

**Discarded by review:**
- **Example House administration** (card 6) — administrators were appointed to Example Office Holdings, owner of Example House, a 45,000 sq ft City of London office bought in 2018 with a five-year bank loan [D186#0]. This matches the revisit trigger in the March 2024 IC note, which declined the building and said to revisit if the owner was forced to sell [D194#2][D194#4]. But the drafted card claimed a £68m decline valuation the evidence doesn't support: the IC note only says the asking price was above the replacement-cost estimate of about £1,250 per sq ft, that the building is EPC F with an ~£11m cost to reach EPC B, and that the tenant paying 62% of rent leaves in 2026 [D194#3]. Worth re-checking once the administrators publish sale terms.
- **Business-rates rise** (card 5) — the Chancellor is weighing a business-rates increase on expensive office blocks and skyscrapers to raise £1bn for the Treasury [D7#0], but the card wrongly placed 99 City Road in City Core (it is City Fringe) and its source attribution wasn't supported, so it was discarded.

**Skipped at triage:** homes (400 build-to-rent homes approved in Croydon [D189#0]), retail (Landsec deprioritising a £1.5bn South London shopping centre plan [D2#0]; Landsec's £516m Metrocentre deal [D72#0]; Chiswick Park lettings [D41#0]), logistics (Blackstone's £1bn industrial loan upsizing [D75#0]), non-London (Cardiff office sale [D44#0]; the FCA relocating to a larger Leeds hub in 2028 [D32#0]; Liverpool's 800-home scheme [D122#0]), and agency-side news (block management expansion [D96#0]; agents chasing deals [D79#0]). Also skipped older refinancings outside the buy box: Battersea Power Station landing a £280m loan from CIMB, OCBC, Maybank and Standard Chartered for its remaining 16 acres [D63#0], and ING and DBS providing £1B to redevelop One Spitalfields' 700K SF with a pre-let secured [D73#0].

**To watch:** the administrators' sale timetable for Example House, and the lender's next move on Example Tower. The pending demand and supply-gap cards cover the rest.
